summary: Practise tender red-flag analysis, bid-rigging screening, and investigation planning with anonymised procurement data. Explore the course.
lede: Procurement fraud analytics helps procurement managers, auditors, investigators, and compliance professionals spot tender risks and plan proportionate reviews. Participants build risk registers, screen bid and supplier data in Excel, and assess indicators such as bid rotation, unusual pricing, repeated awards, and supplier links. They also plan investigations, document and preserve evidence, review controls, and report findings and limitations to decision-makers.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for preventing, detecting, investigating, or overseeing procurement fraud exposure across tendering and contract activity. This course is designed for: Chief procurement officers setting tender integrity controls and escalation routes. Procurement managers reviewing bid evaluations, supplier exceptions, and contract variations. Internal auditors testing procurement controls and documenting control deficiencies. Fraud investigators preserving tender records and developing evidence-based case timelines. Compliance officers reviewing conflicts of interest and procurement-related alerts. Donor-compliance officers checking procurement files against funding and reporting requirements. Public procurement officials assessing bid patterns and supplier eligibility records. Procurement data analysts screening tender and supplier datasets for anomalies. Contract managers monitoring variations, delivery exceptions, and supplier performance concerns. Risk managers maintaining procurement fraud registers and reporting exposure to leadership.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of procurement or internal control processes is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with Excel; Power BI Desktop is optional for the dashboard exercise. The course uses anonymised tender and supplier datasets.
